topic: What operational constraints limit optimal beam-to-beam channel allocation in mesh-type communication when using digital channelizers?
response: The operational constraints limiting optimal beam-to-beam channel allocation in mesh-type communication when using digital channelizers are: (1) preventing more channels being allocated than requested, as stated in equations (27) and (29); (2) satisfying the requirement for beam-to-beam, beam-to-GW, and GW-to-beam communications; and (3) managing multi-valued power allocation due to phased array antenna constraints.
reference_context: The context provides information on flexible resource optimization for geo-multibeam satellite communication systems, including average satisfaction indices for unused offered capacity, unmet system capacity, used bandwidth, and used power. It also discusses digital channelizers, mesh-type communication, and phased array antennas.
